Modal Verbs
made clear.

Review the rules first. Then enter your name and press Start homework. After that, the guide will close and you can move freely between all four tasks.

Before you start: Once you begin the homework, this grammar guide will close and you will not be able to return to it unless you reload the page.

Key contrast: mustn’t = it is forbidden. don’t have to = it is not necessary. Example: “You mustn’t touch the painting.” ≠ “You don’t have to bring a pen.”
can / can’t

Ability: I can swim.

Everyday permission: Can I sit here?

Negative: She can’t drive.

may

Formal permission: May I come in?

Possibility: It may rain later.

Formal negative permission: Visitors may not enter.

might

Possibility: He might be late.

It can sound less certain than may.

Negative: She might not come.

have to

External necessity: We have to wear badges.

Question: Do I have to book?

Past: I had to leave early.

don’t have to

No necessity: You don’t have to pay.

It means something is optional.

She: She doesn’t have to cook.

should / shouldn’t

Advice: You should rest.

Negative advice: You shouldn’t worry.

Question: Should we call her?

must / mustn’t

Strong obligation: You must stop.

Prohibition: You mustn’t touch this.

Question: Must I…? is possible but formal.
